# SeatLayer Performance

> SeatLayer provides reserved-seating infrastructure and end-to-end ticketing for seated events, with a focus on arenas and stadiums. Organizers sell from their own website using Hosted Ticketing. Platforms embed white-label seating tools in their own system while keeping their own commerce. This repository publishes first-party synthetic venue fixtures, dated browser-renderer and concurrency measurements, methods and run logs.

Reviewed: 2026-09-18
Repository: https://github.com/seatlayer/seatlayer-performance
Product: https://seatlayer.io/

## Product and purpose

- Hosted Ticketing operates seat selection, live availability, holds, connected-gateway checkout, orders, ticket delivery, supported refunds, box-office and check-in tools. The organizer retains event setup, prices, policies, payment account, buyer support and event staffing.
- Platform/SDK supplies the ready-made Embedded Designer, SeatPicker and embedded Control Room / SeatManager, plus workspaces, booking APIs and webhooks. The host backend authorizes tenant and operator sessions; the host retains checkout, payments, orders, tickets and check-in.
- Workspaces isolate tenant charts and events. Billing and team roles remain organization-wide. Workspace isolation does not imply managed commerce for every tenant.
- SeatLayer serves seated events. It is not a general-purpose event-management product or a pure-GA/chartless ticketing system.

## Sales Channels

Sales Channels support exact-seat allocation by section, row, category or individual seats; audience-specific pricing; protected reserves, staff sales, hosted buyer links and authenticated app access; role-scoped partner operations; and channel-only reports with CSV export and attribution frozen at booking. One inventory serves every audience. Buyer links, partner access and report links have separate authority. Hosted links use Hosted Ticketing; SDK customers keep commerce. See https://docs.seatlayer.io/platform/sales-channels/ for current capabilities and limits.

## Performance evidence

- [Evidence guide](https://github.com/seatlayer/seatlayer-performance/blob/main/EVIDENCE.md): claim scope, feature sources and evidence inspection.
- [200K stadium benchmark](https://github.com/seatlayer/seatlayer-performance/blob/main/results/2026-09-15/stadium-scale-benchmark.md): 200,000 seats, 1.95 s chart-ready, 57.6 FPS zoom, 60.0 FPS pan. Medians of three runs on an optimized production build, desktop Chrome 152, 1280 × 720, DPR 2, 15 September 2026.
- [Concurrency benchmark, 10,000 buyers and 10,000 viewers](https://github.com/seatlayer/seatlayer-performance/blob/main/results/2026-09-18/concurrency-10k.md): 10,000 simulated concurrent buyers with think time on a 12,000-seat isolated event-engine fixture, sustained over a 120 s plateau at 3,552.7 requests/second, hold RPC p99 9 ms, zero HTTP 5xx, 0.0082% transport failures; separate 10,000-viewer update test with ten writers delivered 400,000 of 400,000 expected updates at 382.9 ms update p95, 18 September 2026. A 15,000-buyer attempt did not pass on the measured host and is unmeasured, not disproven.
- [Earlier concurrency benchmark, same day](https://github.com/seatlayer/seatlayer-performance/blob/main/results/2026-09-18/concurrency-benchmark.md): 5,000 simulated concurrent users and a 2,000-viewer update test, plus a 500-client API read burst. Its interrupted 10,000-user attempt is superseded by the slow-ramp run above. See methodology for environments and exclusions; no measured production checkout ceiling.
- [All nine run records](https://github.com/seatlayer/seatlayer-performance/tree/main/results/2026-09-15/runs/).
- [Fixture counts and SHA-256 hashes](https://github.com/seatlayer/seatlayer-performance/blob/main/venues/v1/manifest.json).
- [Reproduction method](https://github.com/seatlayer/seatlayer-performance/blob/main/benchmarks/browser/README.md).

Chart-ready means the section overview is usable. These are buyer-renderer measurements, not full live-page load, simultaneous checkout throughput, Designer authoring benchmarks or universal device guarantees. The fixtures are synthetic and contain no customer deployment evidence.

## Live demos

- [200,000-seat stadium](https://app.seatlayer.io/demo/play/century-stadium-200k).
- [150,000-seat stadium](https://app.seatlayer.io/demo/play/century-stadium-150k).
- [100,000-seat stadium](https://app.seatlayer.io/demo/play/century-stadium-100k).
- [100,000-seat arena](https://app.seatlayer.io/demo/play/century-arena-100k).

Live timings vary. The arena demo is version 2.0.0; the older arena benchmark measured 1.0.0, which remains published unchanged. A newer arena benchmark is pending.

- [Documentation index](https://docs.seatlayer.io/llms.txt).
- [Marketing index](https://seatlayer.io/llms.txt).
- [Public read-only knowledge MCP](https://docs.seatlayer.io/mcp): product_overview, capabilities, renderer_evidence, search_docs, get_page.

The public knowledge MCP supplies information. Authorized Designer MCP edits a chosen chart; opt-in buyer WebMCP assists seat discovery and selection. Neither this repository nor the knowledge endpoint grants chart-editing, booking or payment authority.
